channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Bitcoin Tops $80,000 as Coinbase and Crypto Stocks Rally | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Jess Menton, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia-Backed Data Center Firm Nscale Files Publicly for US IPO
item.description: Nscale, a developer of artificial intelligence data centers that counts Nvidia Corp. and Microsoft Corp. among its partners, filed for an initial public offering in New York to tap into AI’s insatiable demand for computing power.
item.dc:creator: Subrat Patnaik

item.title: Crusoe CEO: Data Center Indusry Has a 'Marketing Issue’
item.description: Crusoe CEO Chase Lochmiller discusses the AI infrastructure company's nearly $4 billion in fresh funding sending its valuation to almost $31 billion. He also discusses how it will fuel the company’s push to build AI infrastructure spanning data centers, cloud computing and managed AI services. He says Crusoe could eventually enter the public markets and pushes back against growing opposition to data centers, arguing the industry has a “marketing issue” and needs to better communicate its impact on water, jobs and local tax revenue. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former FTC Technologist Warns Against an AI ‘Cartel’
item.description: As frontier AI labs seek greater coordination on safety, Neil Chilson, Head of AI Policy at the Abundance Institute and former FTC Chief Technologist, warns that government-backed antitrust exemptions could create a durable “cartel” that ultimately harms competition. He argues companies can collaborate on safety standards without suspending antitrust rules, and that existing consumer-protection and liability laws already provide tools for addressing harms caused by AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Investor Franklin: AI Safety Concerns Won't Slow Spending
item.description: Calls to “pace” development at the AI frontier are unlikely to translate into a slowdown in infrastructure spending, according to Sara Araghi, Franklin Templeton Portfolio Manager and Franklin Venture Partner. She argues that even if labs temper some model training, growing inference demand will continue to require enormous amounts of compute. Araghi also discusses why heightened AI safety concerns could boost demand for cybersecurity and why she doesn’t expect the debate to derail funding or anticipated AI IPOs. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic's Existential Risk Warnings Hijack Larger AI Debate
item.description: As AI itself starts to help build the next generation of AI, warnings about losing control are growing louder. But critics say the focus on existential risk is overshadowing problems already here. Bloomberg's Rachel Metz and Davey Alba join Ed Ludlow on their latest reporting on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s Claude Takes Bigger Role in Building AI
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Anthropic's finding that its Claude chatbot is leading 26% of its AI research and development, even as the global debate around AI heats up. Plus, SoftBank is closing out the week with nearly $21 billion in potential fresh borrowings as it builds out its AI financing capacity, and Crusoe CEO Chase Lochmiller discusses the race to build the infrastructure powering AI as the company closes nearly $4 billion in fresh funding. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia, Google, Emerald AI Form AI Energy Management Alliance
item.description: Nvidia, Google and Emerald AI have launched the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA), a coalition that dynamically manages the electricity use of data centers in response to grid conditions. Varun Sivaram Founder and CEO of Emerald AI joins to discuss the alliance. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta-Tied Data Center Prices Junk Bond Amid Blowout Demand
item.description: The first junk-bond offering for a data center tied to Meta Platforms Inc. attracted demand more than four times the deal’s size, with juicy yields helping to lure investors.
item.dc:creator: Gowri Gurumurthy

item.title: Buffett Steps Down at Berkshire
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with David Gura on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Tech stocks pare morning gains as the sector’s recovery from a rocky week loses steam, while the S&P 500 turns lower and Brent crude extends its decline. Plus, China tariffs reportedly on hold ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, a changing of the guard at Berkshire, PwC CEO Paul Griggs on AI reshaping jobs, Mbappé’s stunning Nike exit, and new scrutiny of the Fed over SVB. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Disney Names AI Executive as First-Ever Chief Technology Officer
item.description: Walt Disney Co. named Karandeep Anand to the newly created role of chief technology officer for the entertainment giant.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Buckley

item.title: Fire Flares Up at Damaged Moss Landing Battery Storage Site
item.description: Fire crews are responding to a blaze Friday at Vistra Corp.’s damaged battery storage facility in California.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Rosenthal

item.title: Immunology Drugmaker Electra Falls 12% After Upsized US IPO
item.description: Electra Therapeutics Inc., a clinical-stage developer of immunology drugs, dropped 12% in its trading debut Friday after raising $350 million in an upsized US initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Angel Adegbesan

item.title: AI Spend Has Been 'Critical' for US Economy, Says Torsten Slok
item.description: AI hardware continued to drive August’s increase in import prices, as it has throughout the year. Commodity-price volatility from the Iran war raised the cost of industrial materials at the border. Companies face higher input costs and rising expenses tied to the AI buildout. Torsten Slok, Chief Economist at Apollo Global Management, discusses the Fed's rate decision and role AI investment has played in supporting the US economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Newsom Wants AI ‘Kill Switch’ to Rein in Tech Industry
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom issued an executive order on Friday pushing to implement guardrails on artificial intelligence in the state that’s the epicenter of the technology’s boom.
item.dc:creator: Josh Sisco and Andrew Oxford

item.title: Amsted Said to Weigh $6 Billion Sale of Cooling System Unit BAC
item.description: Amsted Industries is exploring a sale of cooling system provider Baltimore Aircoil Co., as strong demand for data center components pushes more owners to test the market, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: David Carnevali

item.title: PWC CEO Rejects AI Job Doom
item.description: PWC CEO Paul Griggs says AI should be viewed as a business transformation, not simply a technology upgrade. He says companies most exposed to AI are seeing stronger productivity and hiring, while PWC itself is adding engineers, data scientists and machine-learning experts as its workforce evolves. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Amazon in EU Crosshairs Over Suspected Price Curbs on Sellers
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. is under scrutiny from the European Union for potentially imposing unfair restrictions on firms selling on its platform.
item.dc:creator: Spencer Soper and Samuel Stolton

item.title: Yahoo Finance and Polymarket End Prediction Market Partnership
item.description: Yahoo Finance has ended a partnership with Polymarket in which the financial news platform used Polymarket data to create a prediction market hub on its website.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Miller

item.title: Pennsylvania’s Josh Shapiro Calls for Tougher AI Safeguards
item.description: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro called for tougher safeguards around artificial intelligence Thursday, wading into a growing debate over the risks of the rapidly advancing technology while arguing the US can continue to reap its economic benefits.
item.dc:creator: Liz Skalka
